title: Explaining complex technical concepts: a guide for technical writers on Mac
metaTitle: Simplification strategy: explaining complex technical concepts for tech writers
description: Learn how to master your simplification strategy for explaining complex technical concepts effectively on your Mac without extra software.
intro: Explaining complex technical concepts requires a balance between deep accuracy and user accessibility. You can improve your output by focusing on task-based structures rather than just shortening your sentences.
tldr: Focus on what the user needs to do instead of what the system does.
Use analogies to anchor new information to things the reader already knows.
Adopt Simplified Technical English principles to reduce ambiguity in your drafts.
Audit your content against actual support tickets to find where users get stuck.
Use Lazur to quickly draft explanations and refine your tone by voice.

blocks.text: When you fail to simplify technical information, the consequences hit your team immediately. Support tickets spike because users cannot find the answers they need in your documentation. Field errors increase when instructions are too dense or ambiguous. This creates a cycle where you spend more time answering the same questions repeatedly instead of building new content.

Technical writers often struggle because they are caught between two worlds. Subject matter experts provide deep, complex data, but users need simple, actionable steps. If you strip away too much detail, you risk inaccuracy. If you keep too much, you lose your audience. This gap often leaves writers relying on trial and error rather than a formal methodology.

items: Task-based writing: Define the user goal first. Do not explain the system architecture until the user has successfully finished their task.
Use analogies: Connect a new, complex concept to a common, physical object or a simple, known process.
Simplified Technical English: Use a restricted vocabulary. Stick to one word for one meaning. Avoid synonyms that confuse the reader.
Content auditing: Look at your support team's most frequent questions. Update the documentation for those specific areas first.
Visual support: Use screenshots with clear annotations to replace long, text-heavy paragraphs.

faq.question: Is there a standard for simple technical writing?
faq.answer: Yes, look into Simplified Technical English (STE) standards like ASD-STE100. It enforces limited vocabulary and strict grammar to keep documentation clear.

faq.question: How do I know if my content is too complex?
faq.answer: Check your support ticket volume. If users ask the same questions repeatedly after reading your docs, the content is likely too complex or misses the mark on user goals.

faq.question: Should I use AI to simplify my writing?
faq.answer: AI is a helpful tool for drafting, but it cannot replace your human judgment. Use it to suggest simpler phrasing, but verify every technical detail against your product specs.

costs.title: Support overhead
costs.text: When documentation fails to simplify, your support team spends hours answering questions that should have been solved by your guide.

costs.title: Operational errors
costs.text: Complex, confusing instructions in the field lead to mistakes that cost time and potentially safety for the user.

causes.title: Domain knowledge gap
causes.text: SMEs know the product perfectly but often cannot translate that knowledge into simple, user-friendly language.

causes.title: Lack of methodology
causes.text: Most writers rely on experience rather than a formal, repeatable process for simplifying content.

fixes.title: Task-based structure
fixes.text: Start every section with the user's goal. Tell them how to do the thing, then explain the system if needed.

fixes.title: Use analogies
fixes.text: Anchor complex technical concepts to real-world objects. This helps the reader build a mental model faster.
